```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

A GBIF snapshot has billions of records in a directory of Parquet files, far more than fits in memory. `flag_occurrences()` takes such a directory, a single file or a vectra query in place of a data frame, reads it in chunks through [vectra](https://gillescolling.com/vectra/), and writes the flags to disk next to the columns kept for grouping. This article walks through the output layout, resuming an interrupted run, tallying from disk, and the one test whose result depends on how the input is split. Installation is covered in [Get started](OccurrenceCleaner.html).

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(OccurrenceCleaner)
```

## Example input

Three `.vtr` files stand in for the parts of a snapshot. Each contains 3,000 records with GBIF's lower-case column names:

```{r input}
set.seed(7)
make_part <- function(n, offset) {
  data.frame(gbifid = as.character(offset + seq_len(n)),
             kingdom = sample(c("Animalia", "Plantae", "Fungi"), n, TRUE),
             species = sample(sprintf("sp%02d", 1:30), n, TRUE),
             year = sample(1880:2024, n, TRUE),
             decimallongitude = round(runif(n, -10, 30), 3),
             decimallatitude = round(runif(n, 36, 60), 3))
}
src <- file.path(tempdir(), "snapshot")
dir.create(src, showWarnings = FALSE)
for (i in 1:3) vectra::write_vtr(make_part(3000, (i - 1) * 3000), file.path(src, sprintf("occurrence-%d.vtr", i)))
list.files(src)
```

A directory of Parquet parts, a single Parquet, `.vtr`, `.csv` or `.tsv` file, and any `vectra_node` are read the same way.

## Flagging into an output directory

For on-disk input, `out` names the output directory and `keep` the columns copied next to the flags. The record identifier (`gbifid` here, set through `occ_columns(id = ...)`) is kept whenever it is present, so the flags can be joined back to the full records later:

```{r flag}
out <- file.path(tempdir(), "flags")
f <- flag_occurrences(src, out = out, keep = c("kingdom", "year"),
                      columns = occ_columns(id = "gbifid"))
f$n
f$parts
```

Each input file is one unit of work. Within a unit, records are read chunk by chunk, flagged, and buffered; a `.vtr` part file is written once at least `part_rows` rows (2 million by default) have accumulated, and at the end of the unit. A `.done` marker per unit records that it finished, and `flags_meta.rds` records the tests, the layout version, the reference, the columns and the package version:

```{r layout}
list.files(out)
m <- read_flagged(out)
str(m[c("tests", "layout_version", "reference", "keep", "n", "units", "package_version")])
```

Memory use is set by the chunk size of [vectra](https://gillescolling.com/vectra/) and by `part_rows`, not by the size of the input: one input chunk and the buffered output rows (the identifier, the `keep` columns and a four-byte flag word per record) are held at a time.

## Resuming

A rerun of the same call skips every unit whose `.done` marker exists. Removing the marker of one unit, as an interruption during that unit would leave it, means only that unit is flagged again:

```{r resume}
file.remove(file.path(out, "occurrence-2.done"))
f <- flag_occurrences(src, out = out, keep = c("kingdom", "year"),
                      columns = occ_columns(id = "gbifid"))
```

A unit that is redone first has its old part files deleted, so a half-written unit never leaves stale parts behind. `resume = FALSE` redoes every unit.

An output directory belongs to one configuration. A rerun into it with different tests, a different reference or land scale, or a different flag layout stops instead of mixing flags:

```{r mismatch, error = TRUE}
flag_occurrences(src, out = out, tests = c("invalid", "zero"), keep = c("kingdom", "year"))
```

## Tallying from disk

`tally_flags()` accepts the `occ_flagged` object or the output directory and streams the parts, so the counts per group of records each test flags and each rule removes are built over the whole snapshot without loading it. Grouping columns must have been kept when flagging:

```{r tally}
cc <- c("zero", "equal", "capital", "centroid", "institution", "gbif_headquarters", "sea")
t <- tally_flags(out, by = "kingdom", bins = list(year = c(1950, 2000)), rules = list(cc = cc))
knitr::kable(t[, c("kingdom", "year_bin", "n", "flagged_sea", "flagged_capital", "removed_cc", "kept_cc")])
```

Most of these records are flagged by `sea`, because the simulated points were drawn uniformly over a box that includes the Mediterranean, the Bay of Biscay and the North Sea. A grouping column that was not kept is an error that names it:

```{r tally-missing, error = TRUE}
tally_flags(out, by = "species")
```

## Reading the flags

`flagged_table()` opens all parts as one [vectra](https://gillescolling.com/vectra/) table. vectra verbs run on it lazily, and `vectra::collect()` brings the result into memory. A vectra query runs once, so each use starts from a fresh `flagged_table()`:

```{r read}
ft <- flagged_table(out)
flagged <- vectra::collect(vectra::filter(ft, flags != 0L))
nrow(flagged)
head(flagged)
```

The flag word is an integer column, so `has_flag()` applies to it after collecting:

```{r read-has}
table(kingdom = flagged$kingdom, capital = has_flag(flagged$flags, "capital"))
```

To attach the flags to the full records, join on the identifier. For a snapshot, the join is best done by vectra on disk; for a small subset, in memory:

```{r join}
recs <- vectra::collect(vectra::tbl(file.path(src, "occurrence-1.vtr")))
fl <- vectra::collect(flagged_table(out))
merged <- merge(recs, fl[, c("gbifid", "flags")], by = "gbifid")
nrow(merged)
```

## Duplicates and the unit of work

`duplicate` compares a record with the earlier records of the same unit. On a data frame the unit is the whole table; on a directory it is one input file, so two identical records in different files are not flagged. A copy of a record from part 1 placed in part 3 shows it:

```{r dupl}
p1 <- vectra::collect(vectra::tbl(file.path(src, "occurrence-1.vtr")))
p3 <- vectra::collect(vectra::tbl(file.path(src, "occurrence-3.vtr")))
copy <- p1[1, ]; copy$gbifid <- "copy-1"
vectra::write_vtr(rbind(p3, copy), file.path(src, "occurrence-3.vtr"))
g <- flag_occurrences(src, out = file.path(tempdir(), "flags-dupl"), tests = "duplicate",
                      columns = occ_columns(id = "gbifid"), verbose = FALSE)
d <- vectra::collect(flagged_table(g))
has_flag(d$flags[d$gbifid == "copy-1"], "duplicate")
```

A table that is split by species, so that all records of one species are in the same file, makes the per-file test equal to the whole-table test, since a duplicate must share the species. A GBIF snapshot is not split that way. For whole-table duplicates on a snapshot, the duplicate test is run on the records of the taxa under study after collecting them, where it sees all of them at once.

## Selecting before flagging

A `vectra_node` is flagged as one unit, which makes it the way to flag a subset without writing it out first. [vectra](https://gillescolling.com/vectra/) pushes the filter down into the scan:

```{r node}
node <- vectra::filter(vectra::tbl(file.path(src, "occurrence-1.vtr")), kingdom == "Plantae")
h <- flag_occurrences(node, out = file.path(tempdir(), "flags-plants"), keep = "kingdom",
                      columns = occ_columns(id = "gbifid"), verbose = FALSE)
h$n
```

## A GBIF snapshot

GBIF's Parquet snapshot (the `occurrence.parquet` directory) names the Darwin Core columns in lower case, which the case-insensitive defaults of `occ_columns()` find. A pass over every test the snapshot supports, which is all but the fossil tests and the range test, keeping the columns a loss analysis groups by. The grouped tests (`outlier` and the two dataset tests, which read `datasetkey`) add a pass over all files before the record pass:

```{r snapshot, eval = FALSE}
f <- flag_occurrences(
  "gbif_snapshot/occurrence.parquet",
  tests = setdiff(flag_tests()$test, c("age_equal", "age_outlier", "spatiotemporal_outlier",
                                       "age_range_outlier", "range")),
  out = "flags",
  keep = c("kingdom", "phylum", "class", "year", "coordinateuncertaintyinmeters"),
  land_scale = 50)

tally_flags(f, by = c("kingdom", "class"),
            bins = list(year = c(1900, 1950, 1970, 1990, 2010),
                        coordinateuncertaintyinmeters = c(10, 100, 1000, 10000)),
            rules = list(cc = cc, cc_country = c(cc, "country_mismatch")))
```

Read through [vectra](https://gillescolling.com/vectra/), the snapshot's `issue` column arrives as a string of issue names separated by `;`, which the issue tests read directly. The in-memory speed of the nine default tests was 17.8 s for ten million records on an AMD Ryzen 7 5700G (`bench/benchmark.R` in the source repository); a streamed run adds the Parquet reading and the writing of the parts, which were not part of that benchmark. Since each Parquet file is one resumable unit, a run over a snapshot can be stopped and restarted at any point and loses at most the file in progress.
